label: An archive worth sharing
summary: Make a start on a book or learning material from work you have collected.
title: AI Coaching for Archives and Personal Projects | GreenElephant
description: Learn to use AI with your notes, interviews or research. Explore an outline and a small sample for a book or learning project, with human coaching.
headline: Turn a lifetime of work into something others can learn from.
intro: You have notes, interviews, films or research worth sharing. Learn how AI can help you organise a small part of it and explore a shape for your book or learning project. You choose the meaning, the audience and the voice.
audience: Researchers, educators, filmmakers and other people with experience or material they want to pass on. You may be starting a new chapter or returning to a project that has waited for years.
example: Choose a small set of material you own or have permission to use. Together, explore recurring themes, keep track of their sources and try an outline. Then test a short passage or lesson to see what fits your intention.
practice: Organising a manageable sample and keeping its source labels.
Asking AI to suggest themes and an outline, then checking them yourself.
Drafting a small sample in a voice you can recognise as your own.
takeaway: An outline and a tested sample can help you decide what to develop next. We agree a realistic scope for the journey; a finished book is a larger project.

faq.question: Do I need to digitise everything first?
faq.answer: Start by discussing the material and its format. We can agree which small, usable sample to bring and what preparation it needs.

faq.question: What happens to private material?
faq.answer: You decide what can be used. We discuss permissions and tool settings before uploading anything; confidential items can stay out of the exercise.

invitation: Tell us about the material—and who you hope it will help.

label: A new business idea
summary: Explore an idea and choose a practical next test.
title: AI Coaching for Your Next Business Idea | GreenElephant
description: Explore a new business idea through personal AI coaching. Clarify a customer problem, draft an offer and plan a small test using your experience.
headline: Explore your next business idea with AI—on your terms.
intro: Bring an idea and the experience behind it. Learn to use AI to ask better questions, explore an offer and prepare a small real-world test.
audience: People considering a small venture after a long career, during a transition or alongside their current work. You do not need a finished business plan to begin.
example: Suppose you want to turn something you know into a service. Use AI to explore who might need it, draft questions for those people and write a first description of the offer. Check the assumptions before deciding what to do.
practice: Turning a broad idea into a clear customer question.
Drafting an offer in words that sound like you.
Preparing one small test and deciding what you want to learn from it.
takeaway: A clearer offer draft, a short list of assumptions and a manageable next experiment. You keep the business decisions; AI helps you explore and prepare.

faq.question: Will AI tell me whether the idea will work?
faq.answer: AI can suggest possibilities, but real people provide the evidence. We help you distinguish a promising suggestion from an assumption that still needs testing.

faq.question: Can I bring an idea that is still rough?
faq.answer: Yes. A question such as “Could my experience help someone with this problem?” is enough for a discovery conversation.

invitation: Bring the idea you keep coming back to.

label: Everyday AI confidence
summary: Learn through useful tasks from your own life.
title: Personal AI Coaching for Everyday Life | GreenElephant
description: Learn to use AI through everyday tasks you choose. Practise asking clear questions, checking answers and keeping control, with patient personal coaching.
headline: Feel more confident using AI in everyday life.
intro: Start with something useful to you: writing a message, planning a personal project or understanding unfamiliar information. Learn at a manageable pace, with a person who helps you ask, try and check.
audience: Adults who want practical help getting started with AI. Your questions and interests shape the work; you do not need a technical background.
example: Bring a letter or a planning task with private details removed. Practise asking for an explanation or a first draft. Compare it with the original, spot what needs checking and make the result your own.
practice: Giving enough context without sharing unnecessary personal details.
Asking follow-up questions when an answer is unclear.
Checking sources and changing a draft so it expresses what you mean.
takeaway: A few repeatable tasks you have practised yourself, plus simple notes to help you try them again.

faq.question: What if I find AI overwhelming?
faq.answer: We start with one task and explain each step. There is room to ask questions and repeat what needs more practice.

faq.question: Can someone else arrange the journey for me?
faq.answer: Talk with us about who will attend and who will pay. The learner helps choose the goal and what they want to share.

invitation: What is one everyday task you would like help with?

label: Facilitation and coaching
summary: Prepare and follow through while keeping your attention on people.
title: AI Training for Facilitators and Coaches | GreenElephant
description: Build a practical AI workflow for preparation and follow-through. Personal coaching for facilitators and coaches who want to keep their attention on people.
headline: Use AI around your work. Keep your attention on people.
intro: Explore how AI can support preparation, writing and follow-up in your professional practice. Keep your own judgement, voice and responsibility for the people you work with.
audience: Facilitators, business coaches and learning designers who want to connect scattered AI experiments into a useful working routine.
example: Take a fictional or approved brief. Use AI to explore a session outline, check whether the activities serve the goal and prepare a follow-up summary. Review what each step adds—and where your attention matters.
practice: Turning a brief into useful preparation questions.
Adapting an outline or exercise to a particular group.
Checking a summary against the source and turning it into clear next steps.
takeaway: A small preparation-to-follow-up workflow you have tried, with clear points for your own review.

faq.question: Is this coaching from an AI chatbot?
faq.answer: Your learning is guided by a human coach. You practise with AI tools as part of your own professional work.

faq.question: Do I need to bring client recordings?
faq.answer: No. Use a fictional, anonymised or explicitly approved example. Client recordings are not needed to learn the steps.

invitation: Which repeatable part of your work would you like to improve?

label: AI in your professional work
summary: Practise with tasks you understand and tools your workplace allows.
title: AI Coaching for Experienced Professionals | GreenElephant
description: Use your expertise as the starting point for learning AI. Practise reports, research or recurring work with personal coaching; discuss employer sponsorship.
headline: Keep your expertise. Build new ways of working with AI.
intro: You know your field. Learn to use AI with the reports, research and questions you already understand, so your experience guides the work.
audience: Experienced specialists who want focused, beginner-friendly practice with relevant tasks. An employer may be organising the learning, or you may be exploring it yourself.
example: Use a public or approved sample report. Ask AI to help structure a summary, identify questions and prepare a repeatable draft. Check each important claim against its source before deciding what is useful.
practice: Giving clear instructions drawn from your own expertise.
Comparing an AI answer with reliable source material.
Building a small working template and a checklist for reviewing its output.
takeaway: A task you have practised end to end, a reusable guide and a clearer sense of where AI helps your work.

faq.question: Can my employer arrange this?
faq.answer: Start with a discovery conversation. We discuss the learning goal, participant needs, scope and fee before a booking is confirmed. Employer payment or reimbursement is not automatic.

faq.question: Can I use workplace material?
faq.answer: Only material and tools your organisation allows. A public, fictional or appropriately approved example can be used for practice instead.

invitation: Bring one professional task you know well and would like to approach differently.
